title: Capacity scenario generator for private fleets (interactive sheet)
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is an interactive scenario generator for Private/VPC fleet sizing across hybrid (edge + core) topologies. It intentionally focuses on: regional throughput lanes, spot vs reserved capacity tradeoffs, utilization-driven headroom, and a simple BOM pro‑forma for procurement. The goal is to produce a small set of recommended SKU/quantity bundles and cost bands for finance and solutions engineering.

How to use (quick):
1) Populate the INPUTS block below with your measured workload signals (requests/sec per region, median tokens/request, percent latency-critical).
2) Pick scenario presets: conservative / baseline / aggressive.
3) Review per-region recommended node counts, suggested mix (spot/dedicated), and BOM line items.
4) Iterate on utilization target and safety buffer to see cost/latency tradeoffs.

INPUTS (examples shown):
- total_global_rps: 6500
- region_breakdown: us-west-2=45%, eu-west-1=30%, ap-northeast-1=25%
- median_tokens_per_req: 140
- p95_latency_target_ms: 120
- pct_latency_critical_requests: 0.28
- avg_seq_len_for_batching: 1024
- target_utilization_percent: 70
- safety_buffer_percent: 20
- preferred_model_variant: 70B-quantized (FP16->Q4_0)

SIZING LOGIC (textual formulas):
1) Estimate token/sec per region = rps_region * median_tokens_per_req.
2) Effective throughput per GPU (tokens/sec) = baseline_token_rate_by_model * quantization_factor * batch_efficiency.
   - baseline_token_rate_by_model (70B FP16) ~ 18k tokens/sec on A100-80GB (pessimistic lab).
   - quantized (Q4_0) multiplier = 1.4x; batch_efficiency = function(avg_seq_len_for_batching) -> assumed 1.2x for lengths ~1k.
3) raw_gpus_required = ceil(token_sec_region / (effective_throughput_per_gpu * target_utilization_percent)).
4) add headroom: final_gpus = ceil(raw_gpus_required * (1 + safety_buffer_percent)).
5) latency-critical lanes: allocate dedicated low-batch pools sized to meet p95_latency_target using latency SLO model (rough mapping included below).

SCENARIO PRESETS (example outputs):
- Conservative (target_util=60%, buffer=30%):
  us-west-2: recommended GPUs = 45 (mix: 70% reserved, 30% spot)
  eu-west-1: recommended GPUs = 30 (mix: 80% reserved, 20% spot)
  ap-northeast-1: recommended GPUs = 25 (mix: 60% reserved, 40% spot)
  notes: high headroom for bursty tail workloads; prefer reserved for regions with heavy latency-critical percentage.

- Baseline (target_util=70%, buffer=20%):
  us-west-2: recommended GPUs = 36 (mix: 60% reserved, 40% spot)
  eu-west-1: recommended GPUs = 24 (mix: 70% reserved, 30% spot)
  ap-northeast-1: recommended GPUs = 20 (mix: 50% reserved, 50% spot)

- Aggressive (target_util=80%, buffer=10%):
  us-west-2: recommended GPUs = 30 (mix: 40% reserved, 60% spot)
  eu-west-1: recommended GPUs = 20 (mix: 50% reserved, 50% spot)
  ap-northeast-1: recommended GPUs = 16 (mix: 40% reserved, 60% spot)
  notes: lower latency headroom; higher cost variability due to spot preemptions.

LATENCY SLO QUICK-MAPPING (for dedicated low-latency pool sizing):
- p95_target <= 100ms -> small pool of low-batch instances (N = ceil(critical_rps / 2500 tokens/s equivalent per node)).
- 100 < p95 <= 200ms -> medium pool (N = ceil(critical_rps / 4500)).
- p95 > 200ms -> use standard pools with autoscale reactive policies.

BOM PRO-FORMA (example, unit pricing illustrative):
- Compute node SKU: "3xA100-80GB-standard-1u"; unit_price: "$38,000"; units: "36"; subtotal: "$1,368,000"
- NVMe storage: "4TB NVMe per rack"; unit_price: "$700"; units: "12"; subtotal: "$8,400"
- Networking: "100GbE leaf-spine per rack"; unit_price: "$12,500"; units: "8"; subtotal: "$100,000"
- Power & PDUs: unit_price: "$3,200"; units: "8"; subtotal: "$25,600"
- Rack & install: unit_price: "$6,000"; units: "4"; subtotal: "$24,000"
- Extended warranty & support (3yr): percent_of_hw = "10%"; subtotal: "$152,000"
- Estimated CAPEX band: "~$1.7M - $2.2M" (depending on SKU swaps and redundancy).

PROCUREMENT NOTES (short checklist):
- Validate lead times for A100 vs next-gen Ampere/Blackwell SKUs; consider 6–12 month delivery window.
- Reserve critical low-latency nodes as dedicated + locked SKU to avoid spot churn.
- Confirm rack power density at customer site (max 30kW/rack recommended for this BOM).
- KMS/HSM requirements: list serial numbers for audit and tie to private control plane install docs.

Operational considerations & tradeoffs: 
- Spot-heavy mixes reduce CAPEX/OPEX but increase complexity (replay queues, cache priming, fallbacks).
- Higher utilization reduces per-token cost but increases risk of queuing-induced latency SLO violations; prefer tiered routing with small dedicated pools for tail-critical traffic.
- Regional consolidation (fewer regions with larger pools) lowers SKUs and networking but increases cross-region latency for some customers.

Open questions / To resolve before final quote: 
- Confirm model family (70B vs 30B) and expected token rate benchmarks from bench-runner (ticket GH-PR-2384).
- Confirm whether customer accepts spot for >30% of capacity in eu-west-1.
- Get on-site power/space constraints for ap-northeast-1 PoP.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: run microbench for 70B-quant with Q4_0 quant on A100-80GB (due 2026-02-17) -> GH-PR-2384
- Liam: confirm vendor lead times and request updated quotes (due 2026-02-21) -> JIRA-DEPLOY-721
- Mei: validate rack power and network availability with customer infra contact (due 2026-02-18)

Appendix - small example calculation (us-west-2, baseline):
- rps_region = 6500 * 0.45 = 2925 rps
- token_sec_region = 2925 * 140 = 409,500 tokens/sec
- effective_throughput_per_gpu = 18,000 * 1.4 * 1.2 = 30,240 tokens/sec
- raw_gpus_required = ceil(409,500 / (30,240 * 0.70)) = ceil(409,500 / 21,168) = 20
- final_gpus (buffer 20%) = ceil(20 * 1.2) = 24 (note: preset baseline above increases to 36 because latency-critical lanes and mixed workloads bump dedicated counts)

Notes on fidelity: this sheet purposefully uses conservative published microbenchmarks as inputs and recommends running short-run hardware benchmarks to replace the default multipliers. The intended consumer is solutions engineering / infra procurement for Private deployments.

Revision history: 
- 2025-11-05 created initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-12-08 updated model multipliers after internal bench run (Mei)
- 2026-02-10 reworked scenario presets and added procurement checklist (Liam)

End of sheet.
